title: reverseproxy: replace only known placeholders in health check body
body:
Fixes #7021. Implements @mholt's suggestion in that thread ("We could probably switch to replacing only known placeholders"), scoped to the body.

### Problem

The active health check body is expanded with `repl.ReplaceAll`, which blanks any `{...}` the replacer doesn't recognise. Only globals are available here, so a JSON `health_request_body` is sent as an **empty body**:

```
reverse_proxy 10.0.0.2:80 {
	health_request_body `{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"eth_blockNumber","params":[]}`
}
```

The header values three lines below already use `ReplaceKnown`, so the two halves of the same request were built with different rules.

This isn't limited to bodies without placeholders. A body that **does** use one is mangled too — `{"token":"{env.SOME_VAR}"}` goes out as `"}`, because the opening `{"token":"` is consumed as an unrecognised placeholder before the real one is reached. Both are in the tests.

### Fix

One line: `ReplaceAll` → `ReplaceKnown` for the body. Unrecognised braces are left intact; real placeholders still expand.

### Scope: why the `Host` header is deliberately left alone

I said on the issue that I'd change `Host` on line 454 too, since it uses `ReplaceAll` while the header values below it use `ReplaceKnown`. Testing showed that would make it worse, so I didn't.

Go's HTTP server blanks a `Host` containing braces — sending `Host: {not.a.placeholder}` to an `httptest` server, the handler sees `r.Host == ""`. That's stdlib behaviour. So today `ReplaceAll` blanks an unknown placeholder and Go falls back to the URL host and the request works; `ReplaceKnown` would leave the literal `{...}` in `req.Host` and the upstream would discard it. Happy to revisit if you read it differently.

### Tests

Two cases in `active_health_test.go`, built on the existing `newActiveHandler`/`runActiveHealthCheck` harness:

- a JSON body arrives intact
- a body containing `{env.…}` still has the placeholder expanded

Both fail on `master` and pass with the change:

```
--- FAIL: TestActiveHealthCheckBodyKeepsUnknownPlaceholders
    health check body = "", want "{\"jsonrpc\":\"2.0\",...}"
--- FAIL: TestActiveHealthCheckBodyStillReplacesKnownPlaceholders
    health check body = "\"}", want "{\"token\":\"s3cret\"}"
```

`go test ./modules/caddyhttp/...`, `go vet` and `gofmt` are clean.

### Disclosure

Per CONTRIBUTING: this was written with AI assistance (Claude). I can explain every line, and the behaviour of both the fix and the `Host` finding above was verified by running the tests, not inferred.
